# Arulnidhi Karunanidhi

Arulnidhi Karunanidhi is an AI evaluations and research engineer working on LLM and agent evaluations, adversarial model behaviour, scorer robustness, memory poisoning, and agentic AI safety.

## Research interests

- **LLM and agent evaluations:** constructing reproducible evaluations for model-graded, stateful, and multi-agent systems, including work with Inspect AI.
- **Adversarial model behaviour:** testing safety-relevant behaviour under controlled attacks, trust-boundary violations, and agent–tool failure conditions.
- **Scorer robustness:** examining whether model graders and deterministic scorers measure the intended construct across prompt, model, context, and repeated-run variations.
- **Memory poisoning and long-context evaluation:** measuring how false facts, provenance, retrieval policy, and context construction affect downstream agent behaviour.
- **Agentic AI safety:** producing bounded, reproducible evidence about the capabilities and failure modes of agentic AI systems.

## Projects

### Aegis Memory

[Aegis Memory](https://github.com/quantifylabs/aegis-memory) is a scope-aware persistent-memory system and an experimental substrate for studying isolation, provenance, retrieval, long-context behaviour, and memory-poisoning risks in multi-agent systems.

### Evaluation robustness

Ongoing evaluation research tests model grading, scorer failure modes, adversarial variants, meaningful baselines, and sensitivity to prompts and context policies. Numerical claims are published only when a directly accessible benchmark artifact supports them.

## Writing

- [Evaluating the Evaluator: What a Broken Scorer Taught Me About LLM Evals](https://arulnidhii.github.io/posts/evaluating-the-evaluator/) — an experiment comparing deterministic, model-graded, and lexical methods, with scorer failure analysis and follow-up tests.
- [Scope-Aware Memory Access Control for Multi-Agent Systems](https://arulnidhii.github.io/posts/scope-aware-memory-access-control.html) — a case study of memory boundaries, threat modeling, and failure testing in a multi-agent system.
